tools.name: search
tools.description:
Finds the tools of the servers below by running JavaScript: write an async arrow function, such as async () => { ... }. It runs in a sandbox with no network or file access; what it returns comes back as JSON, after anything it wrote with console.log. Return only what is needed: output longer than about 24000 characters is cut.

In the code:
- codemode.servers(): Promise<{ id: string, description: string, upstream: boolean }[]>
- codemode.groups(server: string): Promise<string[]>, the groups a large server is split into (empty when it is not)
- codemode.tools(server: string, group?: string): Promise<{ id: string, description: string, inputSchema: object }[]>, the tools of one group, or of the whole server

Example:
async () => {
  const tools = await codemode.tools("git:github", "repos");
  return tools.filter((tool) => tool.id.includes("branches")).map(({ id, description }) => ({ id, description }));
}

Servers:
- security:bitwarden: Bitwarden password manager through its own MCP server (github.com/bitwarden/mcp-server), cloned on first use into ~/.usemcpkit/repos/security/bitwarden, built there and run locally: vault items, folders, attachments, Send, password and TOTP tools. Needs git, Node.js and npm on PATH, the Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) for the vault tools, and a vault unlocked with its `unlock` tool (a native password dialog; BW_SESSION, BW_CLIENT_ID and BW_CLIENT_SECRET from the client's env are passed along when set). It reads and changes real credentials, so allow only the tools you trust.
- productivity:clickup: ClickUp REST API (v2 and v3): tasks, checklists, comments and custom fields, the Workspace hierarchy (spaces, folders, lists, views), time tracking, goals, users and guests, chat, docs, webhooks and audit logs. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'. The v2 endpoints call the Workspace id `team_id`; list the Workspaces with hierarchy:workspaces:get_authorized_workspaces.
- cloud:cloudflare: The Cloudflare API through Cloudflare's own remote MCP server (github.com/cloudflare/mcp, mcp.cloudflare.com), in code mode: search the OpenAPI spec and run API calls from JavaScript, so every product (Workers, KV, R2, D1, Pages, DNS, firewall, load balancers, Access and more) is reachable through a few tools, plus Cloudflare documentation search and whoami. `execute` can change or delete anything the token allows, so give the token only the permissions you want the AI to have.
- atlassian:confluence: Confluence REST API for Cloud and Data Center. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>': group cloud is Cloud REST v2 (/wiki/api/v2), cloud_v1 is Cloud REST v1 (/wiki/rest/api) and datacenter is Data Center / Server REST (/rest/api); call the group that matches the configured host.
- communication:discord: Discord HTTP API v10, called as a bot: channels, messages, reactions, threads and pins, guilds (members, roles, bans, emojis, stickers, scheduled events, auto moderation, audit logs), users and DMs, application commands, webhooks, invites and lobbies. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'. Ids are snowflakes passed as strings; list the bot's guilds with users:guilds:list_my_guilds.
- design:figma: Figma REST API: files and their nodes, rendered images and image fills, versions, comments and reactions, dev resources, published components, component sets, styles and variables, library analytics, teams' projects and folders, webhooks and the current user. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'. A file key is the part after /design/ in a Figma link, and a node id looks like 1:2 (a link carries it as node-id=1-2). files:files:get_file returns the whole document and can be enormous: prefer files:files:get_file_nodes with ids, or pass depth. Variables need an Enterprise plan; operations that need an OAuth app or an organization token are not included.
- git:github: GitHub REST API: repositories, issues and pull requests, Actions, security, organizations, users, apps, Copilot and meta endpoints. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'.
- git:gitlab: GitLab REST API (gitlab.com and self-managed): projects, issues and merge requests, CI/CD, packages, security, groups, users, administration, AI and meta endpoints. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'.
- atlassian:jira: Jira REST API (Cloud and Data Center): issues, projects, users, workflows, fields, dashboards and filters, administration, apps and Jira Software boards and sprints. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>' and use the /rest/api/2 endpoints (Jira Software: /rest/agile/1.0), so endpoints that exist only on Cloud fail on Data Center. Issue search picks the endpoint of the deployment.
- communication:medium: Medium's API (api.medium.com/v1), which Medium has archived and no longer supports: it needs an integration token you already have, since Medium stopped issuing new ones. Get the authenticated user (account:me:get_me), list their publications and a publication's contributors, publish posts as HTML or Markdown to the profile or a publication (as a draft, unlisted or public), and upload an image. The API cannot read, edit or delete posts. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'. `posts:posts:create_*` publishes under the token owner's name, so prefer publishStatus draft.
- automation:n8n: n8n public REST API of an n8n Cloud or self-hosted instance: workflows (create, update, publish, activate, archive, transfer, history, tags), executions (list, read, retry, stop), evaluation test runs, credentials and credential type policies, data tables with their columns and rows, projects with their folders, members and variables, users, roles and role mapping rules, instance settings (LDAP, SSO, log streaming, OpenTelemetry, security and node type policies), the security audit, community packages, source control, insights and environment promotions. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'. Which tools work depends on the instance's plan and version and on the API key's scopes; enterprise features answer 403 without a license. Deprecated operations are not included.
- api:postman: Postman through Postman's own remote MCP server (github.com/postmanlabs/postman-mcp-server, mcp.postman.com) in its Full mode: workspaces, collections with their folders, requests, responses, comments, forks and pull requests, environments, mock servers, monitors, specs, the API catalog, governance rules, SDKs, teams and search. Tools that create, change or delete act with the API key's permissions.
- communication:reddit: Reddit's OAuth API (read-only): a subreddit's posts, a post with its comment tree, search for posts and subreddits, subreddit info and rules, user profiles and their posts and comments. Tools are named '<group>:<resource>:<action>'. Posts and comments are identified by fullnames (t3_<id>, t1_<id>); listings page with `after` set to the last item's `name`.
- communication:teams: Microsoft Teams through the community MCP server by Inditex (github.com/InditexTech/mcp-teams-server), cloned on first use into ~/.usemcpkit/repos/communication/teams, set up with uv and run locally on a Python that uv installs for it (the system Python is never used). It works in the one team and channel it is configured for: start a thread, reply to it, read a thread or the channel's threads, and look up team members to mention. It signs in as a Microsoft Entra application (a bot) and needs git and uv on PATH. The first call opens a form for TEAMS_APP_ID, TEAMS_APP_PASSWORD, TEAMS_APP_TENANT_ID, TEAM_ID and TEAMS_CHANNEL_ID (or set them in the client's env for usemcpkit). It posts as the bot into a real channel, so allow the write tools only when you want that.
